title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Strong magnetic anisotropy is not restricted to macrocyclic ligands: enlarging and rigidifying the side chains of the flexible open-chain ligand PyMTA can tune lanthanide magnetic anisotropy.
explanation: The review explicitly says this overturns the view that strong anisotropy requires macrocycles. Separately, NO3−- and CO32−-induced pentagonal and hexagonal subunits build hollow truncated-tetrahedral 3d–4f clusters whose hollow architecture raises magnetic density and magnetocaloric performance of a Gd–Ni cluster.
scope: Lanthanide complexes of open-chain PyMTA-type ligands and hollow 3d–4f clusters for magnetism or magnetic refrigeration.
conditions: Larger, more rigid coordinating side chains on PyMTA; hollow cluster architectures from NO3− and carbonate subunits.
caveats: The macrocycle exception and the magnetocaloric hollow-cluster result are distinct examples and should not be merged into one structure–function rule.
